anya p.: Quick sync — onboarding candidate rdx-v3-medium (FP16 -> int4 sweep) is ready for smoke/regression gates. I pushed a canary prompt suite + 3 bucketing groups (commonsense, instruction-follow, code-gen). Need alignment on pass criteria and whether we run full quant sweep now or after smokes. cc @carl m. @sam_k

carl m.: thanks. high level: smoke = correctness + safety fast check (~500 samples), regression = larger benchmark + prompt perturbations. pass if fail-rate delta < 1.5% and semantic-similarity drift < 0.03 on embed metric. :white_check_mark:

sam_k: +1 to that baseline. also want latency SLO check under continuous batching: p95 < 220ms for our default tokens. If quantized, measure both p95 and tail after 30s steady QPS.

mei zhang: added a small eval script to ri-eval to capture topk-token-overlap and embedding-drift. snippet:```bash
ri-eval run --suite onboarding_canary --model rdx-v3-medium-quant4 --buckets commonsense,instruction,code 
# produces metrics.json with: topk_overlap, embed_cosine_delta, safety_hits
```

anya p.: perfect. can we decide thresholds? proposal: topk_overlap >= 0.88 vs fp16 baseline, embed_cosine_delta <= 0.025, safety_hits <= baseline + 0.5% (absolute). If any bucked fails smoke, hold rollout.

carl m.: embed threshold looks fine. topk 0.88 might be tight for code-gen; drop to 0.85 for code bucket, keep 0.88 for others. safety is absolute counts not percent for small sets — use absolute pad of +3 examples for low-frequency safety checks.

sam_k: for regression runs (full harness): require BLEU/ROUGE-ish style deltas: relative drop < 2% for instr-follow tasks, semantic-acceptance (human QA) pass rate delta < 1.5 pts. Also, ensure quantized model doesn't increase hallucination tokens per 1k tokens by > 5.

anya p.: noted. operational gating question: do we run quant sweep (int4 dynamic vs static, per-channel) in canary or after a canary pass? My vote: canary with one representative quant config (dynamic int4) then full sweep in dedicated bench cluster if pass. avoids noisy failures.

mei zhang: agree. canary = single quant config + safety/lint smoke. full sweep = matrix of {int4-dyn,int4-stat,int8} x {KV-cache-enabled,KV-cache-disabled}. run per-bucket. schedule full sweep on dedicated nodes to avoid interfering with prod.

anya p.: rollout policy: canary->staged A/B (5% then 30%) with automatic rollback if any model variant exceeds delta thresholds or if latency SLO breached. Who owns the rollback play? @carl m.?

carl m.: I can own rollout. also add a watchdog alert in console: if per-route error-rate > 0.5% or p95 latency regresses by > 40ms for 3 consecutive mins -> auto-fallback to previous pinned model. deploy-bot: please capture that.

deploy-bot: captured rollout policy in ticket #INF-1942 and scheduled canary window 03/30 22:00 UTC.

evalbot: smoke run queued: job id ev-87921. expected finish ~12m. results link: https://internal.redwood/evals/ev-87921 (will post metrics when done).

sam_k: one more: include prompt perturbation ensemble in smoke (synonym swaps, prefix truncation, temperature jitter) — helps catch brittle regressions.

anya p.: added perturbation set to the canary suite. thanks everyone. next: when ev-87921 finishes, post metrics here and we decide run vs sweep. :thumbsup:
